liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (1 review): The transition from Jack Straw to Cold Rain And Snow was well executed [3]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): The sequence from Dark Star through Black Muddy River was described as pretty epic [9]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): Eleven and Not Fade Away teases appeared within the St. Stephen performance [3]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Diamonds On The Soles Of Her Shoes began during the final two minutes of Wheel [3]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): The second set featured extended jams, with Wharf Rat being a massive highlight [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **Deep Elem Blues**: rare: 6 archived performances [10]
- **Jack-A-Roe**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [10]
- **Diamonds On The Soles Of Her Shoes**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [10]

## The recordings

- **DeadCo2018-06-01.travitz.schoepsMK4v.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 4.75/5 by 8 [1]

## Around the show

- The atmosphere in the venue was fun with good vibes [4]
- A party occurred over the weekend, with attendees discussing summer plans [5]
- Oteil was subdued but focused, while he and Mickey performed impressively [6]
- The reviewer had good seats, allowing for a close view of the band [6]
- John was channeling Jerry, while Jeff was channeling Brent during the performance [7]
- The reviewer attended their first show since seeing Phil and Merl at Central Park [8]
- This performance is considered the best Dead and Company show the reviewer has heard [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **DeadCo2018-06-01.travitz.schoepsMK4v.flac16**: taped by Jeff Travitz; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: Schoeps MK4V's>KCY 250/5i>Schoeps VST5u>SD744t [1]. Also: Jeff Travitz and Keith Litzenberger handled the recording and sharing of the file; Recorded using Schoeps MK4V microphones, a KCY 250/05i preamp, and a Sound Devices 744T [1][5]
